faq.a: Tahira is associated with the Arabic form طَاهِرَة, whose core sense is tahira; pure, chaste (feminine).

faq.q: What is the origin of Tahira?
faq.a: Tahira is associated with Arabic. Tahira is Arabic طَاهِرَة (Ṭāhira), the feminine of طَاهِر, meaning 'pure, chaste'.
Yes — the underlying form طَاهِرَة is Arabic.
Tahira can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Tahira should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Ṭāhira is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Tahira mean in Persian?

faq.a: Romanization variants include Tahira, tahira. Script forms are طاهره, طاہرہ, طَاهِرَة, ताहिरा.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
